title: Sigeumchi Namul
subtitle: Seasoned blanched spinach
excerpt: A simple Korean side dish of blanched spinach dressed with garlic, sesame oil, and soy sauce. It takes ten minutes to make and is one of the most common banchan on a Korean table. The key is blanching the spinach quickly and squeezing out every drop of water before seasoning.
sourceNotes: Sigeumchi namul is one of the foundational banchan of Korean home cooking, appearing in lunchboxes, at family meals, and as a component of bibimbap across the country. The technique of blanching, squeezing, and seasoning leafy greens is centuries old and applies equally to spinach, watercress, and other soft vegetables.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Can be made up to a day ahead. Keep covered in the fridge and bring to room temperature before serving.

glossaryTerms.definition: Namul is the Korean term for a category of seasoned vegetable side dishes. Raw or cooked vegetables are dressed with a combination of soy sauce, sesame oil, garlic, and other aromatics. Namul dishes form a central part of banchan, the small side dishes that accompany rice at a Korean meal.

content.text: This recipe serves 4 as a side dish and is ready in 10 minutes. Sigeumchi namul is a classic Korean

, a seasoned vegetable dish made by blanching spinach and dressing it with garlic, sesame oil, and soy sauce. It is one of the first side dishes many Korean home cooks learn, and it appears on the table almost daily.

The single most important step is squeezing the spinach thoroughly after blanching. Any water left in the leaves will dilute the seasoning and make the dish watery. Use your hands and squeeze hard in small batches. The spinach should feel quite dry before the dressing goes on.
Bring a large pot of water to the boil. Salt it lightly.
Add the spinach and blanch for 30 to 45 seconds until just wilted. Drain immediately into a colander.
Rinse under cold running water to stop the cooking. Leave for a minute to cool completely.
Gather the spinach into a ball and squeeze firmly with both hands. Repeat in small handfuls until as dry as possible. Roughly chop into 5cm lengths.
Place the spinach in a bowl. Add the soy sauce, sesame oil, garlic, and spring onions. Toss well with your hands or chopsticks.
Scatter sesame seeds over the top and serve at room temperature or chilled.

items.symptom: The spinach is watery and the seasoning tastes diluted
items.cause: The spinach was not squeezed dry enough after blanching
items.fix: Tip the spinach back into a clean cloth or kitchen paper and squeeze again firmly before re-seasoning

items.symptom: The spinach tastes raw or slightly bitter
items.cause: The blanching time was too short
items.fix: Blanch for a full 45 seconds. The spinach should be fully wilted with no raw texture remaining

items.cause: Soy sauce brands vary in saltiness and residual water in the spinach can concentrate the seasoning
items.fix: Start with half a tablespoon of soy sauce, toss and taste before adding more

content.text: Sigeumchi namul is a staple of the Korean table. It appears as one of the small side dishes at everyday meals and is also a key filling in bibimbap. The technique is identical for many other vegetables including bean sprouts, watercress, and fernbrake. Once you know how to make this, the same method works across a whole family of Korean side dishes. It keeps well in the fridge for a day and is often made in advance as part of a spread of banchan for the week.
